item.description: Texas Longhorns guard Isaiah Johnson (2) dribbles the ball during the game against Southern Indiana at the Moody Center on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Longhorns point guard Isaiah Johnson played just four minutes in Sunday's 97-61 win over Southern Indiana after his "butt tightened up" during pregame warm-ups, per head coach Sean Miller. Horns247's Eric Henry reported Johnson suffered a "glute strain." Miller told the media in Austin postgame he didn't know the severity of Johnson's injury. "We were precautionary," Miller said. "We got a lot of repetitions and we had different people in different roles," Miller said Sunday. "It was good for our team. item.title: Glenn Schumann is set to be FSU football's next coach. What's his recruiting track record?
item.description: It turns out the man partially responsible for the beginning of Mike Norvell's downfall is set to become Florida State 's next football coach. Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann is expected to be named Florida State's next head football coach , USA TODAY Sports John Brice reported Monday, Nov. 23. The Glenn Schumann-coached Georgia defense coasted to a 63-3 win over the Seminoles in the 2023 Orange Bowl on Dec. 30, 2023. Just more that 1,000 days later, Schumann is set to replace Norvell, who was fired on Nov. 1. Schumann, 36, did not play college football, but enrolled at Alabama to work under legendary head coach Nick Saban in 2008. He worked in various roles under Saban and then-defensive coordinator Kirby Smart before following Smart to Athens, Georgia, as the inside linebackers coach in 2016. Schumann was promoted to co-defensive coordinator with now-Oregon coach Dan Lanning in 2019 and then served as co-defensive coordinator with Will Muschamp before being promoted to the full-time role in 2024, shortly after the blowout win vs. FSU. After the struggles Norvell had as a recruiter with the Seminoles , FSU fans may wonder about Schumann's experience and track record on the recruiting trail. Well, Schumann has helped the Bulldogs sign 14 five-stars during his time with the program. Here is a look at the five best players Schumann served as a primary recruiter for: Raylen Wilson, 5-star linebacker (2023) Schumann hails from Valdosta, Georgia. That being only about 75 miles northeast of Tallahassee, Florida, helped his connection with Wilson, the No. 28 overall player in the 2023 recruiting cycle. The relationship between Schumann and Wilson helped the Bulldogs pluck Wilson from Lincoln High School in Tallahassee to and send him to Athens instead of staying home with the Seminoles. Remember, at this time, FSU and Norvell were riding the high of coming off a 10-3 season. While Wilson is not the highest-ranked recruit Schumann added in his time at Georgia, he's been productive for the Bulldogs, tallying 102 career tackles, 8.5 sacks, three forced fumbles and an interception. Now the head coach at Florida State, keeping those relationships with Tallahassee-area programs will be key for Schumann. Nolan Smith, 5-star edge rusher (2019) The former five-star recruit out of IMG Academy (Bradenton, FL) lived up to expectations as the No. 1 overall player — according to 247Sports Composite rankings — in the 2019 recruiting cycle. Schumann played the primary recruiting role for Smith, who now plays for the Philadelphia Eagles, in his first recruiting cycle with the Bulldogs. Smith finished with 114 total tackles, 21 tackles for loss and 11.5 sacks in his time in Athens. Following four years with the Bulldogs — a span that included two national championships — Smith was the No. 30 overall pick by the Eagles in 2023 NFL Draft. item.title: 2027 Five-star CJ Rosser commits to UNC
item.description: Clarence CJ Rosser Jr., #14 of the United States of America (USA) in action during the FIBA U17 Basketball World Cup - Turkiye 2026 Group A match between the United States of America (USA) and France at Basketball Development Centre in Istanbul, Turkey on June 27, 2026. (Photo by Altan Gocher / Hans Lucas / AFP via Getty Images) | Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images Today it was announced that 2027 five-star power forward CJ Rosser has committed to the University of North Carolina. This announcement is the second that Michael Malone has earned from the 2027 class so far, and it has given the Tar Heels potentially their best recruiting class in over a decade. Breaking: CJ Rosser, the No. 3 ranked player in the SC Next 100 for the Class of 2027, has committed to North Carolina, he announced. pic.twitter.com/M4AjKwhi4U — SportsCenter NEXT (@SCNext) November 23, 2026 There was a lot of speculation that Rosser was ready to announce his commitment, but the signs weren’t particularly clear. He had canceled an official visit to Kentucky, and around that time On3’s Joe Tipton had changed his crystal ball to favor the Tar Heels. Rosser is a 6’10, 200-lb power forward from Orlando, FL. He currently players for Southeastern Prep, and he is considered the second-best player in the country according to the 247Sports Composite Rankings . Rosser chose the Tar Heels over Miami, NC State, Arkansas, Kentucky, USC, and Louisville. Scouting reports indicate that Rosser is an inside-out player that has a lot of athleticism and defensive potential. It’s fair to say that some of the things being said about him aren’t far off from what we heard about Caleb Wilson, which is that he’s an inside-out player that is still kind of raw but has a lot of upside. Social media has been calling Rosser “Baby KD,” referring to current Houston Rockets star, Kevin Durant. Checking out some of his moves on the court paints a pretty vivid picture as to why he earned the moniker. View Link This is incredible news for Michael Malone and his staff, and for the Carolina fan base as a whole. The Heels have now earned commitments from two top-five players, one of whom has officially signed in Demarcus Henry. The best part is that Malone still isn’t finished — word on the street is that UNC is still in play for Beckham Black, and Jalen Davis, who currently has UNC in his top four, plans to announce where he is attending school tomorrow. There’s a lot more actively going on with Malone’s recruiting board, but ultimately this was the best news that could’ve been delivered right before UNC’s game against Monmouth. item.title: Tigers Emerge as Potential Landing Spot for Former All-Star Pitcher
item.description: The Detroit Tigers may have another intriguing name to consider as they look to strengthen their starting rotation for the 2027 season. According to MLB Network insider Jon Paul Morosi, former Kansas City Royals All-Star Kris Bubic is among the free-agent pitchers who could make sense for Detroit this offseason. The 29-year-old left-hander is coming off a season that included a trade to the Los Angeles Dodgers, an injury-related absence, and a return in time for postseason action. Now a free agent, Bubic could represent an opportunity for Tigers president of baseball operations Scott Harris to add a pitcher with considerable upside without necessarily committing to a lengthy contract. Oct 4, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Kris Bubic (40) reacts after being relieved during the fifth inning against the Atlanta Braves in game two of the NLDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) MLB Insider Names Tigers as Potential Kris Bubic Destination During a November 18 appearance on MLB Network, Morosi discussed Bubic’s free-agent market and identified Detroit as one of several potential landing spots. His comments, also highlighted by MLB.com’s November 19 rumor roundup , suggest the Tigers could be an appealing destination for the former Royals standout. “So again, teams like the Royals who know him well, the Tigers who would like to get a shorter-term starting pitcher, Cubs, Orioles, [Blue] Jays, and the Cardinals as well,” Morosi explained. That is an interesting development for Detroit, especially considering the organization’s need for additional pitching depth. However, it is important to distinguish Morosi identifying the Tigers as a potential fit from a report confirming that Harris has entered negotiations with Bubic. Detroit has already been connected to other free-agent starting pitchers, including former Chicago Cubs All-Star Shota Imanaga . Adding Bubic to the discussion gives Tigers fans another name to monitor as the club attempts to put together a more dependable rotation. What Kris Bubic Could Bring to Detroit Bubic’s appeal begins with his ability to perform at a high level when healthy. During the 2025 season with Kansas City, he earned his first American League All-Star selection after posting an impressive 2.55 ERA across 20 starts and 116⅓ innings. His success was not limited to that one season, either, as MLB.com’s examination of his free-agent market noted that Bubic has recorded a 2.90 ERA over the past three seasons while working in both starting and relief roles. That performance makes him an intriguing candidate for teams seeking upside in the free-agent market. However, durability remains a legitimate concern. item.title: Fernando Mendoza gave Raiders a glimpse of their future with ownership after loss
item.description: Alex Singleton had spent Sunday afternoon trying to make Fernando Mendoza’s first NFL road start as miserable as possible. By the time it was over, the Broncos linebacker sounded like a man who understood Denver had better enjoy days like this against the Raiders quarterback while it could. “He’s a first-round pick, first overall for a reason,” Singleton said. “He’s going to be a good player.” And that was after the Broncos tagged Mendoza for five sacks. Imagine what Singleton might say someday when the kid has time to throw. Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) throws against the Denver Broncos in Denver, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/Jack Dempsey Mendoza earned the compliment. Playing without Brock Bowers, his best receiver, in a stadium loud enough to cost the Raiders an early timeout, he threw three touchdown passes. Patrick Mahomes is the only other visiting quarterback to do that in Denver this season. Matthew Stafford managed two. Sam Darnold and Trevor Lawrence left town without one between them. Mendoza also joined Lawrence and Joe Burrow as the only quarterbacks drafted first overall to throw for at least 250 yards and three touchdowns in a game within their first two career starts. Somewhere down the line, maybe Mendoza will appreciate the company he kept Sunday. In Denver, he seemed more interested in a cornerback named Ja’Quan McMillian. And that might be the best news the Raiders brought home. “Don’t get me wrong, although I believe it was an improvement, there are a lot of things I need to improve on for next week,” Mendoza said. Denver Broncos’ Alex Singleton (49) sacks Las Vegas Raiders’ Fernando Mendoza (15) during a game in Denver, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Getty Images Take the throw that McMillian returned for a touchdown. If you want to understand the distance Mendoza traveled in a week and how much ground he still has to cover, listen to him explain what happened in the instant before he let that ball go. “I saw him take a shuffle inside – thought he was walling another slant – and I let it go with anticipation, and he made a fantastic play,” Mendoza said. A week earlier against Seattle, Mendoza was trying to see the entire field. In Denver, he picked up a cornerback shuffling inside, understood what that movement usually meant for a different receiver, and threw to the spot he expected to come open. McMillian got a hand on the ball. All that processing, and the guy who wound up in the end zone played for Denver. The easy thing would have been to tip his cap and leave it there. Mendoza was considering what a checkdown over the middle might have bought him. A few yards. Another down. A chance for his defense to catch its breath. item.title: Texas State football grades: Bobcats continue to roll in win over Washington State
item.description: Texas State football trailed 7-0 in the opening minutes of its Saturday contest against Washington State. The Bobcats locked in for the rest of the game, scoring 42 unanswered points and winning 42-14 in the final regular-season conference game. Despite finishing second in the Pac-12 standings, Texas State will miss the championship game after San Diego State upset Boise State on Saturday night. The Aztecs hold the tiebreaker over the Bobcats, having defeated them 31-29 in October. Here are the grades from Texas State's win. Offense: A- Texas State continued to dominate on the ground, racking up 299 yards on 45 attempts for an average of 6.6 yards per attempt. Running back Torrance Burgess Jr. led the backfield with 146 yards and a touchdown on 19 attempts, led by another dominant performance from the offensive line. Quarterback Brad Jackson threw for 122 yards and a touchdown on 11-of-19 passing. He did most of his damage with his legs. Jackson sliced open the Cougars' defense, rushing for 127 yards and three touchdowns on nine attempts. Wide receiver Beau Sparks led the team with four receptions for 39 yards and a touchdown. item.title: Texas defensive back Kobe Black out for rest of season with knee injury but Hero Kanu could return
item.description: Texas defensive back Kobe Black (6) is out for the rest of the season with a knee injury. (Jason Fochtman/Staff photographer) AUSTIN - Texas safety Kobe Black has been ruled out for the rest of the season, but defensive tackle Hero Kanu could possibly return to the team in the playoffs after his arm surgery a week ago, Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said on Monday. Asked if there's any chance Kanu could get back after surgery for a torn biceps, Sarkisian smiled and said, "Potentially. I'll use that word." Black, who was moved from cornerback in the offseason and played 341 snaps, left Saturday's game against Arkansas early with a knee injury. His absence will deprive Texas of one of its top backups. "I hate it for him," Sarkisian said. "It's disappointing. He was having a really good year for us with the position change. But the other guys need to step up." item.title: Boston Celtics at Washington Wizards: Stream, lineups, injury reports, broadcast (11/24)
item.description: The NBA regular season can be like a roller coaster. The Boston Celtics currently find themselves on the part of the ride that points straight down — except there's no fun in this steep drop. The C's have lost four games in a row, which is enough for their longest losing streak since the 2020-21 campaign. They'll look for a reprieve in the regular-season roller coaster on Tuesday night, when they face the Washington Wizards in D.C. It's no secret that the Celtics have had the Wizards' number in recent years. They've beat their Eastern Conference foe 11 consecutive times, with the last win for the Wizards dating back to March of 2023. But, these aren't the same Wiz the C's have crushed in the past. Washington has prevailed in three straight contests after a slow start to the season and seems to have found a stud in forward AJ Dybantsa, the first overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft (and a former Celtics fan who grew up less than an hour outside of Boston). Meanwhile, the Celtics are reeling and need to play desperate in the nation's capital to avoid going 0-4 on their rough road trip. Records, standing, and streaks The Celtics have lost four games in a row and, for the moment, sit in third place in the Eastern Conference with an 11-6 record. The Wizards have won three games in a row and own a 7-11 record. They're just barely in Play-In Tournament territory, as they hold ninth place in the East. Player injuries For the third consecutive night, Celtics center Mitchell Robinson is out with an illness. As for the Wizards, Reece Beekman (right AC joint sprain), Justin Champagnie (right foot surgery), Tristan Vukcevic (left hip impingement), and Jamir Watkins (left ACL repair) are out on Tuesday evening. Two-way center Felix Okpara is listed as questionable. item.description: The Los Angeles Rams could be in for a rude awakening for their Thanksgiving Eve game against the Green Bay Packers. With the game set to kick off on Wednesday night, teams sent in their final injury reports and the Packers revealed that edge rusher Micah Parsons will be making his season debut against the Rams. Green Bay Packers linebacker Micah Parsons speaks with Los Angeles Dodgers staff members before a game at Dodger Stadium on Monday, April 27, 2026. Kevork Djansezian for CA Post It’s been nearly 12 months since Parsons tore his left ACL against the Denver Broncos in December of last season, and the three-time All-Pro has been steadily working his way back by thoroughly rehabbing his injured knee. Since his rookie debut in 2021, Parsons has been a force to be reckoned with on opposing offensive lines, with five consecutive seasons where he registered over 12 sacks. Parsons’ highest number of sacks in a season came in 2023, when he tallied 14 for the Dallas Cowboys. Verstappen, ever the showman, followed it up with a hilarious tirade against rival George Russell, who dared to engage in a war of words with motorsport’s pettiest man. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
